newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey man steals bus to drive himself home.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey man steals bus to drive himself home.

text.p: A do-it-yourself bus driver stole a public bus and picked up some passengers along the way as he tried to get home from northern New Jersey, police said Wednesday.

He started by stealing a 40-foot commuter bus from a NJ Transit garage in Orange, N.J., before dawn, police said. He then stopped to pick up a few passengers -- and charged them the correct fares, police said.
David Middleton, 34, of Egg Harbour Township got as far as this semi-rural suburb in Camden County before he was arrested by Hammonton police.

Hammonton police Lt. Robert Jones said his patrol cars spotted the bus leaving the Garden State Parkway some 100 miles to the south of where Middleton started. They chased the bus into neighbouring Winslow.
"He said he needed a ride home," Jones said.
Middleton was charged with theft, eluding police and driving without a license. He was in the Atlantic County Jail, unable to post $25,000 bail.
NJ Transit was studying how Middleton was able to avert security at the bus yard, said spokesman Steve Coleman.
